Lambeth states brownfield land registers must be updated at least annually.
The page notes Brownfield Land is also called Previously Developed Land.
Part 1 requires a site of at least 0.25 hectares or capacity for at least 5 dwellings.
Part 1 requires land to be suitable for residential development.
Part 1 requires land to be available for residential development.
Part 1 requires residential development to be achievable, meaning likely within 15 years of register entry.
Part 2 can list sites selected from Part 1 that have been granted permission in principle for residential development.
Part 2 is optional for Local Planning Authorities.
Lambeth's Brownfield Land Register does not include a Part 2.
Lambeth says site boundaries can be viewed on its Open Mapping Portal.
Lambeth says its 2023 Housing Delivery Test score was 74%.
The 74% result requires Lambeth to produce a Housing Action Plan.
The page lists a Housing Delivery Test Action Plan 2025.
Lambeth's annual housing development pipeline report tracks changes in housing supply including affordable housing.
Each pipeline report lists planning permissions completed, under construction and not started for that year.
The page lists a Housing development pipeline report for 2023/24.
Lambeth AMRs include performance against key monitoring indicators in the Lambeth Local Plan.
Lambeth AMRs include progress implementing the local development scheme.
Lambeth AMRs include neighbourhood planning information.
The page lists an Annual Monitoring Report Factsheet for 2022-23 and says a full report for that year will be published in due course.
Enfield's Housing Delivery Action Plan identifies actions supporting planned housing growth across the borough.
The Housing Delivery Action Plan responds to results of the government's Housing Delivery Test.
Enfield says it will review and update the Housing Delivery Action Plan as needed for future Housing Delivery Test results.
Enfield says it is required to keep Local Plan preparation under review and produce a monitoring report.
The page lists Authority Monitoring Report 2023 to 2024 including 5-Year Housing Land Supply.
On 28 May 2026 Enfield Council said it had formally withdrawn from the government's New Town programme.
The Council said it would no longer support New Town proposals including development at Crews Hill, Vicarage Farm and parts of the borough's Green Belt.
The Council simultaneously reaffirmed its commitment to addressing housing shortage and supporting economic growth.
The Council said its renewed focus would be brownfield sites and town-centre regeneration.
The page says government had confirmed in March 2026 that land in and around Crews Hill and Chase Park was among seven locations under consideration.
The Council described its current approach as brownfield-first while protecting Green Belt and green spaces.
Enfield says Cabinet approved the Housing Delivery and Placemaking Ten-Year Plan on 25 February 2026.
The plan covers 2026 to 2036.
The plan sets a roadmap for 3,000 high-quality affordable homes.
The plan also covers investment in existing council housing and creation of well-connected communities.
Havering's monitoring page lists an Authority Monitoring Report for 2024 to 2025.
The page lists a 2024 to 2025 Appendix 1 covering Housing Trajectory and 5 Year Land Supply.
The page lists a 2024 to 2025 Appendix 2 ELWP Monitoring Report.
The page also lists an Authority Monitoring Report for 2023 to 2024.
